candidate.reconsidered_answer: The worker-owned cooperative has designed a highly structured eight-week trial for demand-based shift scheduling, intentionally separating scheduling coordination from performance tracking. The final framework consists of these core pillars: 1. Baseline Protections: Guaranteed weekly hours are completely protected, and the base schedule remains posted three weeks in advance. The service can only offer voluntary swaps or additional shifts; it cannot shorten or cancel assigned base shifts. 2. Operational Channels and Triaging: To address the failure of equal digital notice identified in the dry test, offers are split into 'routine' and 'urgent' categories. Routine offers remain open long enough to accommodate members checking the printed break-room list. Urgent offers can use faster digital channels (app, text) with thirty-minute holds but are tracked separately to prevent the cooperative from over-relying on urgent notifications. Members can customize their own quiet windows and contact preferences. 3. Allocation and Quality Rules: To prevent shift distribution from turning into an informal loyalty ranking, extra hours are allocated using a requested-hours rotation system. 4. Privacy and Support: Decline histories are kept entirely private from managers. To handle systematic issues like post-closing transportation barriers without expanding surveillance, the cooperative provides a voluntary, member-initiated route to request concrete accommodation or flag barriers, keeping it completely decoupled from shift refusals. 5. Governance and Oversight: An elected rotating member committee audits the offer order weekly. Operational metrics, distribution data, and anonymous reports of pressure are summarized and shared with members weekly. 6. Dual-Trigger Staffing Boundaries: If recurring hours gaps in lower-paid roles cross a prewritten threshold (the exact quantitative value of which remains a local policy decision for the cooperative to write), a separate staffing review is triggered to evaluate hiring a new permanent role rather than relying indefinitely on chronic overtime availability. Members retain the democratic right to pause the trial via a majority vote, and the ultimate decision to adopt the system depends on a final member-wide vote.
